lines.text: Step three: start a scan. There are three tabs: Ready scan, Template, and Own words.
Ready scan: one tap on Run fills the conditions and runs them on your list. You can change every condition afterwards.
Template fills the conditions, and nothing runs until you press Run.
Three templates are always there: Momentum, Oversold, and Trend on the daily. The names are only labels for the conditions.
Own words, where switched on, turns an idea typed in plain words into conditions you can check. Anything ATP cannot read is listed, never guessed.
See all ready scans opens the screen library.
Filter it by method and by setup, then open a card to fill the conditions.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
Step four: the conditions. Every condition is a block, under the line All of these must pass.
A stock matches only when every switched-on block is true for it. Each underlined part can be changed: the function, its numbers, the comparison.
To add a block, first pick its kind.
Indicator compares a number. Filter is a yes or no check, such as a candle pattern. Category compares a label, such as a trend. Rank keeps the top of your list. Group means either, or.
Then press Add a condition.
A new row appears. Change any underlined part, or switch the block off with its tick box.
Information and education only, not investment advice.

scenes.title: Bars ago and the timeframe chip

lines.text: Each side of a row has a small timeframe chip. Pick another timeframe to read that side on it, for example Daily while the scan runs on 15 minutes.
The small arrow at the row's end opens its advanced options.
Bars ago reads a candle further back: a whole number from 1 to 500. Blank means the last closed candle.
Here the RSI is read three bars ago, and the row says it in plain words.
Some functions, such as structure and patterns, are read on the last bar only. They take no bars ago and no other timeframe.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
